mainTopic: Public executions, the source for delaying capital verdicts, why there are no capital trials on ערב שבת, and whether burying a מת מצוה overrides שבת
overview: This amud opens with more verses about public executions. Two cases are the bodies of שאול's descendants, guarded by רצפה, and the command after בעל פעור to 'take the heads of the people.' רב explains that the leaders were not punished. They were made into many courts so the sinners could be judged quickly and God's anger would turn away. Next the גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that a guilty verdict in a capital case must wait until the next day. רבי חנינא learns it from 'צדק ילין בה' and רבא learns it from 'אשרו חמוץ'. Each one uses the other's פסוק for a different lesson, including that holding back ready-to-eat צדקה overnight on a fast day is like spilling blood. The גמרא then shows why capital trials cannot start on ערב שבת: every possible schedule breaks some rule. Finally, ריש לקיש begins a קל וחומר that burying a מת מצוה should override שבת. The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא on the נזיר verse to prove it, and the ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רצפה guards the bodies from the start of the harvest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the verse about רצפה בת איה spreading sackcloth on the rock from the beginning of the harvest. This shows that the bodies of שאול's descendants stayed exposed for a long time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'And רצפה daughter of איה took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on the rock, from the beginning of the harvest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another verse to the story it is already discussing. The verse shows that the bodies of שאול's descendants were left out in the open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רצפה sat on the rock from the start of the harvest and guarded the bodies, as the rest of the verse describes. So the bodies were not taken down right away. This is a public execution that lasted a long time.

keyTerms.meaning: Rizpah daughter of Aiah, the mother of two of שאול's sons who were executed
Sackcloth, rough cloth worn or used in mourning
Rock
The beginning of the harvest

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And Rizpah daughter of Aiah took
the sackcloth and spread it out for herself
upon the rock, from the beginning of the harvest.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: ״וַתִּקַּח רִצְפָּה בַת אַיָּה אֶת הַשַּׂק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the verses about the execution of שאול's descendants that the גמרא was discussing before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That the bodies of שאול's descendants remained exposed for a long time

steps.title: Why were the leaders punished when the people sinned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the command after בעל פעור to 'take all the heads of the people.' It asks why the leaders should suffer if only the people sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'And ה׳ said to משה: Take all the heads of the people.' If the people sinned, what did the heads of the people do wrong?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case of public execution, from the time of בעל פעור. It points out a problem: the verse seems to punish leaders who never sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain reading suggests the leaders themselves were to be hanged. But the verse never says that the leaders sinned. Punishing innocent people makes no sense, so the reading has to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: The heads (leaders) of the people
They sinned
Take

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And the Lord said to Moses:
Take all the heads of the people.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:4. The verse continues 'and hang them before ה׳,' which is why it sounds like the leaders were being punished.

phrases.english: If the people sinned,
what did the heads of the people sin?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָעָם חָטְאוּ, רָאשֵׁי הָעָם מָה חָטְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of שאול's descendants to a second case of public execution, at בעל פעור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of במדבר 25:4, that the leaders were to be hanged
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the people sinned, so it is unfair to punish the leaders.

steps.title: The leaders were made into courts
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב explains that 'take the heads' means God told משה to set up courts from the leaders. They were not being punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to משה: Divide them into courts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by reading the verse differently. The leaders were taken to be judges, not to be punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Take the heads' now means 'use the leaders.' Each one set up a court to judge the sinners, so the ones who were hanged were the sinners, not the leaders. This removes the unfairness from the last step.

keyTerms.meaning: Divide or distribute
Courts (more than one בית דין)
The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses,
divide courts for them.
phrases.notes: So 'take the heads' means use the leaders as judges for the sinners, not hang the leaders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the leaders would be punished.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leaders themselves were to be hanged.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leaders were appointed as many courts to judge the sinners.

steps.title: Why were many courts needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why several courts were needed. It suggests that a court may not judge two capital cases in one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you say it is because a court does not judge two people in one day...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב's answer needed many courts instead of one. It suggests a possible reason, and this sets up the next step, which will test that suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a known rule that a court does not judge two capital cases on the same day. If that rule applied, one court would have needed many days for all the sinners, so many courts would be needed. The גמרא offers this reason only to check it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will likely be rejected)
A court does not judge two capital cases in one day

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If you say it is because they do not judge
two in one day?
phrases.notes: He means two capital cases, cases where the punishment is death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם שֶׁאֵין דָּנִין שְׁנַיִם בְּיוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why several courts were needed rather than one

steps.title: רב חסדא limits the one-case-a-day rule
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the rule against judging two cases in a day applies only to two different kinds of death penalty. Everyone at בעל פעור deserved the same death, so this rule cannot be the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב חסדא say: They taught this only about two different kinds of death penalty, but for one kind of death penalty, they do judge [several in one day]!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested reason by quoting רב חסדא. His statement shows the rule does not apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, a court may judge many cases in one day if they all carry the same death penalty. The sinners at בעל פעור all did the same sin and got the same punishment. So one court could have judged them all together, and the rule does not explain why many courts were needed.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] say? (introduces a challenge from a known statement)
They taught this only about...
Kinds of death penalty given by a court

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chisda say:
They taught this only about two kinds of death penalty,
but for one kind of death penalty, they do judge!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reason suggested in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that many courts were needed because of the one-case-a-day rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule only covers different kinds of death penalty. At בעל פעור all the sinners got the same one.

steps.title: Many courts so God's anger would turn away quickly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that many courts were set up so the sinners would be judged quickly and God's burning anger would turn away from ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was so that the burning anger would turn away from ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first reason was rejected, the גמרא gives the real reason: speed. Many courts working at once would finish quickly and turn away God's anger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words come from the same verse, which says the execution would make God's anger turn away. The anger would stay until the sinners were dealt with. So many courts were needed for speed, not because of a court rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the correct answer after rejecting another)
Burning anger (of God)
That it should turn away

steps.whatToRemember: At בעל פעור the leaders were not punished. They served as many courts, and the reason was speed: to judge the sinners fast so God's anger would leave ישראל.

phrases.english: Rather, so that it should turn away,
the burning anger, from Israel.
phrases.notes: These words come from the end of the same verse, במדבר 25:4.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּשׁוּב חֲרוֹן אַף מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reason after the first suggestion was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Many courts were set up so the sinners could be judged quickly and God's anger would turn away from ישראל.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the one-day rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that monetary cases may be concluded on the same day, and asks where this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said monetary cases can be finished on the same day, and so on. From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה and asking for its source. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה's rule. In דיני נפשות a court may acquit on the same day, but must wait until the next day to convict. The גמרא wants a פסוק behind this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Monetary cases
They may finish the case on that same day
From where are these things learned?

phrases.aramaic: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת גּוֹמְרִין בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Monetary cases may be concluded on that same day, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, after the בעל פעור discussion ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for finishing monetary cases in one day while delaying guilty verdicts in capital cases.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's source: justice that waits overnight
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא brings the פסוק 'מלאתי משפט צדק ילין בה', which links justice with staying overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: the פסוק says, 'She was full of justice, righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question with a פסוק from ישעיהו about ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ילין' means 'lodges overnight.' רבי חנינא reads the פסוק as praising a city where justice waited overnight before a death sentence. When that stopped, the judges became like murderers. So capital convictions need a delay.

keyTerms.meaning: Lodges overnight, stays the night
Murderers

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
For the verse says,
"She was full of justice, righteousness lodged in her,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:21. 'Lodged' means stayed overnight, and that is the key word here.

phrases.english: "but now murderers."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is 'צדק ילין בה': justice in a capital case should 'lodge overnight' before a conviction.

steps.title: רבא's source: praise the judge who delays
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a different פסוק, 'אשרו חמוץ', and reads it as praising a judge who lets his verdict wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says it comes from here: 'אשרו חמוץ', meaning praise the judge who lets his verdict 'ferment' (who delays it).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second source for the same rule, using a play on words in a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In its plain meaning, 'אשרו חמוץ' means 'help the oppressed.' רבא connects 'חמוץ' to חמץ (leavening, letting something sit). He reads it as 'praise (אשרו) the judge who lets his verdict sit and ferment.' That is a source for delaying a capital conviction.

keyTerms.meaning: Plainly 'relieve'; here read as 'praise'
Plainly 'the oppressed'; read as connected to fermenting or delaying
Lets his verdict 'ferment', delays his ruling

phrases.english: And Rava says it is from here:
"Relieve the oppressed"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:17. רבא is about to read these words in a new way.

phrases.english: Praise the judge who lets his verdict ferment.
phrases.notes: 'Ferment' means he lets the ruling sit a while before announcing it, like dough rising.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different source for the same rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is 'אשרו חמוץ': praise the judge who delays his verdict.

steps.title: How רבי חנינא reads רבא's verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא reads 'אשרו חמוץ' as 'help the one robbed, not the robber.' So he does not need it for delaying verdicts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי חנינא) reads it: 'help the one who was robbed', and not the robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי חנינא did not use רבא's פסוק: he reads it with a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא reads 'חמוץ' (the one robbed) against 'חומץ' (the robber). The פסוק tells judges to side with the victim, not the robber as corrupt judges did. Since he uses the פסוק for that lesson, he cannot learn the delay rule from it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other אמורא)
The robber, the one who oppresses

phrases.english: And the other one:
phrases.notes: This means רבי חנינא. The גמרא is asking how he reads רבא's פסוק.

phrases.english: "Relieve the one robbed," and not the robber.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ וְלֹא חוֹמֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי חנינא does not accept רבא's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חנינא uses 'אשרו חמוץ' to teach that judges must help the victim, not the robber.

steps.title: What does רבא do with רבי חנינא's verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבא uses 'מלאתי משפט', since he did not learn the delay rule from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבא): what does he do with this פסוק, 'She was full of justice'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same question from the other side. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every פסוק teaches something. If רבא does not use 'מלאתי משפט' for the delay rule, he must use it for another lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (How does he use this פסוק?)

phrases.english: And the other one,
what does he do with this verse, "She was full of justice"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, הַאי מְלֵאֲתִי מִשְׁפָּט מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror question of step 10, now about רבא.

steps.title: Holding back charity on a fast day
steps.stepSummary: רבא uses the פסוק for רבי אלעזר's teaching in the name of רבי יצחק: leaving צדקה overnight on a fast day is like spilling blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי אלעזר's teaching in the name of רבי יצחק: any fast day on which the צדקה is left overnight, it is as if one spilled blood. As it says: 'She was full of justice, righteousness lodged in her (but now murderers).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא reads the פסוק as being about צדקה left overnight, not about courts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'צדק' as צדקה and 'ילין' as holding it overnight. Poor people fast all day expecting צדקה to buy food to break their fast. If the צדקה waits until the next day, they are harmed, and that is why the פסוק ends with 'murderers.'

keyTerms.meaning: A fast day
Leave overnight, delay until the next day
Charity
Spills blood

steps.confusionAlert: Both אמוראים read the very same פסוק. They do not focus on different words. They read the same words differently: for רבי חנינא, 'צדק ילין' is justice in court waiting overnight, while for רבא it is צדקה (charity) being held overnight.

phrases.english: Like the teaching of Rabbi Elazar in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תַּעֲנִית שֶׁמְּלִינִין בּוֹ אֶת הַצְּדָקָה –
phrases.english: Any fast day on which the charity is left overnight,
it is as if one spills blood,
as it is said: "She was full of justice, righteousness..." etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא reads the פסוק as teaching that leaving צדקה overnight on a fast day is like spilling blood.

steps.title: The charity rule applies only to ready-to-eat food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the teaching: it applies to bread and dates, not to money, wheat or barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies to bread and dates. But with money, wheat and barley, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבי אלעזר's teaching, explaining exactly when delaying צדקה is so serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread and dates can be eaten right away to break the fast, so delaying them truly hurts the hungry poor person. Money, wheat and barley still need buying, grinding or cooking. So they would not help him break his fast that night anyway, and holding them overnight is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread
Dates
Money (coins)
We have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: Monetary cases may finish in one day, but a guilty verdict in a capital case waits overnight. רבי חנינא learns this from 'צדק ילין בה'. רבא learns it from 'אשרו חמוץ' and uses 'צדק ילין בה' to teach that holding back ready-to-eat צדקה overnight on a fast day is like spilling blood.

phrases.english: And this applies to bread and dates,
but with money, wheat, and barley,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּרִיפְתָּא וְתַמְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the teaching just quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Delaying צדקה overnight on a fast day is like spilling blood only for food ready to eat, such as bread and dates, not for money or raw grain.

steps.title: Why no capital trials on ערב שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule against judging capital cases on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Therefore, we do not judge capital cases on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה and asks why that rule is true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה links this rule with the word לפיכך ('therefore') to the earlier rule that a guilty verdict in a capital case must wait until the next day. The גמרא wants to see exactly how that earlier rule leads to banning trials on ערב שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore. This rule follows from the one before it.
What is the reason?
Etc. The quote is cut short.

phrases.english: Therefore, we do not judge, etc.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ אֵין דָּנִין כּוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the next-day verdict rule means no capital trials on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב.

steps.title: Because there is no workable schedule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is impossible, and asks how we would even try to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is not possible. How would we do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its short answer, 'it is not possible,' and then sets up a list of schedules it will test one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the headline answer. The question 'how would we do it?' starts a step-by-step test, and each schedule will fail for a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible.
How should we act? An opening to test the options.
Because.

phrases.english: Because it is not possible.
How should we act?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר. הֵיכִי לֶיעְבַּד?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 in short and opens the list of options.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No schedule works, as the next steps will show.

steps.title: Option 1: Start and finish on Friday
steps.stepSummary: Judge and finish the whole case on ערב שבת? No, because if they lean toward guilt they must wait overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we judge him on ערב שבת and finish his case on ערב שבת? Maybe they will see a reason to find him guilty, and then they must hold off the verdict until the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first schedule, doing everything on Friday, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An acquittal could be finished on Friday, but a guilty verdict needs הלנת דין, which means waiting overnight. The court cannot know ahead of time which way the case will go, so finishing on Friday is not safe.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב שבת, Friday.
A reason to find him guilty.
Holding off the verdict overnight.

phrases.english: Should we judge him on Shabbat eve
and finish his case on Shabbat eve?
Perhaps they will see a reason to find him guilty,
and they will need to hold off the verdict overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִידַיְּינֵיהּ בְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא וְלִיגְמְרֵיהּ לְדִינֵיהּ בְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First option tested under 'how should we act?'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Doing the whole trial on Friday.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A guilty verdict needs הלנת דין, so it cannot be finished the same day.

steps.title: Option 2: Finish and execute on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Judge on Friday, give the verdict and execute on שבת? No, executing does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we judge him on ערב שבת, finish on שבת, and execute him on שבת? No. An execution does not push aside שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries giving the verdict and carrying out the execution on שבת, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This would fix the overnight wait, but a court execution is not allowed on שבת. So the plan breaks a different rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Killing. Here it means a court execution.
Pushes aside, overrides, שבת.
Let us kill him, execute him.

phrases.english: Should we judge him on Shabbat eve
and finish on Shabbat, and kill him on Shabbat?
Execution does not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדַיְּינֵיהּ בְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא וְלִיגְמְרֵיהּ בְּשַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second option, after option 1 failed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An execution does not override שבת.

steps.title: Option 3: Execute Saturday night
steps.stepSummary: Execute right after שבת at night? No, executions must be done in daylight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we execute him at night, after שבת? No. We need it to be facing the sun.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries executing on מוצאי שבת at night, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This would avoid both the long wait and breaking שבת. But an execution must take place during the day, so night does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: At night, in the evening.
Facing the sun, meaning by day.
We need, we require.

phrases.english: And should we kill him at night?
phrases.notes: He means right after שבת ends, before Sunday morning.

phrases.english: We require 'facing the sun.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיקְטְלֵיהּ לְאוּרְתָּא? נֶגֶד הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בָּעֵינַן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes option 2 to avoid שבת by executing at night.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An execution must be done by day.

steps.title: Option 4: Verdict on שבת, execute Sunday
steps.stepSummary: Give the verdict on שבת and execute on Sunday? No, that makes the condemned man suffer while he waits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we finish his case on שבת and execute him on Sunday? Then you are making his judgment drag on and torment him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries giving the verdict on שבת and waiting to execute until Sunday, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a man is sentenced, the execution should not be held off. Making him wait overnight until Sunday knowing he will die is cruel, so the delay after the verdict is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the week, Sunday.
Making his judgment drag on and cause him suffering.
You turn out to be (doing something wrong).

phrases.english: And should we finish his case on Shabbat,
and kill him on Sunday?
You turn out to be dragging out his judgment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיגְמְרֵיהּ לְדִינֵיהּ בְּשַׁבְּתָא, וְלִיקְטְלֵיהּ בְּחַד בְּשַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next option after night execution failed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Waiting between the verdict and the execution.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It drags out the condemned man's suffering.

steps.title: Option 5: Start Friday, finish Sunday
steps.stepSummary: Judge on Friday and give the verdict on Sunday? No, the judges will forget their reasons over the break.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we judge him on ערב שבת and finish on Sunday? They will forget their reasons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries putting off the verdict until after שבת, and rejects it because the judges will forget their reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This avoids every earlier problem, but the break is too long. The judges' reasons could be lost by Sunday.

keyTerms.meaning: Their reasons will be forgotten.
Let us finish, conclude, it.

phrases.english: Should we judge him on Shabbat eve
and finish it on Sunday?
Their reasons will be forgotten.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִידַיְּינֵיהּ בְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא וְנִגְמְרֵיהּ בְּחַד בְּשַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last option to test.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Putting off the verdict across שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Judges forget their reasons over a long break.

steps.title: The scribes' notes don't solve forgetting
steps.stepSummary: Even though scribes write down who acquits and who convicts, people still forget the reasons in their hearts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though two court scribes stand before the judges and write down the words of those who acquit and those who convict, they only write what is said out loud. A person's heart forgets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא heads off a possible objection: the scribes' written record should prevent forgetting. It answers that it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the written record keeps the reasons safe over שבת. The גמרא answers that the scribes only record spoken words, but the judge's own understanding and reasoning can still fade.

keyTerms.meaning: The judges' scribes, court clerks.
Those who vote to acquit.
Those who vote to convict.
Granted that, even if.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּשְׁנֵי סוֹפְרֵי הַדַּיָּינִין
phrases.english: Even though two scribes of the judges
stand before them,
and write the words of those who acquit
and the words of those who convict,
granted, they write what is in the mouth,
but the heart of people forgets.
phrases.notes: A play on words: אִינְּשֵׁי means 'people' and אִינְּשִׁי means 'forgets.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דִּשְׁנֵי סוֹפְרֵי הַדַּיָּינִין עוֹמְדִים לִפְנֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the rejection in step 20 against the idea that the scribes' notes prevent forgetting.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the counter-idea does not fully work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scribes' written record should keep the reasons safe until Sunday.
steps.terutzMaskana: Writing records only words. The judges' inner reasoning is still forgotten.

steps.title: Conclusion: It's impossible
steps.stepSummary: Since every schedule fails, a capital trial cannot begin on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up: no schedule works, so the משנה rules out capital trials on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the opening answer from step 15, now proven option by option. Each schedule broke one of these rules: הלנת דין, no execution on שבת, execution by day, no suffering while waiting, and not forgetting the reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore, so.

steps.whatToRemember: No capital trial on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב, because every possible timing breaks a rule: הלנת דין, no execution on שבת, execution only by day, no waiting after the verdict, and judges forgetting their reasons.

phrases.english: Therefore, it is not possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ לָא אֶפְשָׁר.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of options.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Capital cases cannot be started on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב because no workable schedule exists.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Does burying a מת מצוה override שבת?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש begins a קל וחומר: Temple service overrides שבת, and burying a מת מצוה overrides Temple service, so maybe burial should override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: Burying a מת מצוה should override שבת by a קל וחומר. Temple service overrides שבת, yet burying a מת מצוה overrides Temple service, as we learn from ״וּלְאַחֹתוֹ״.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. ריש לקיש starts building a קל וחומר, and the גמרא pauses partway through to bring the source for the middle step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain is: מת מצוה is stronger than עבודה, and עבודה is stronger than שבת, so מת מצוה should be stronger than שבת. The idea that מת מצוה beats עבודה comes from ״וּלְאַחֹתוֹ״. The גמרא now stops to quote the ברייתא that explains this before ריש לקיש finishes his argument.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead body with no one else to bury it.
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one.
The Temple service.
'Or for his sister.' The פסוק about a נזיר.

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש's sentence is not finished here. The 'so surely it overrides שבת' ending comes after the גמרא brings the ברייתא for ״וּלְאַחֹתוֹ״.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Let the burial of a met מצוה
override Shabbat by an a fortiori argument:
If Temple service, which overrides Shabbat –
the burial of a met מצוה overrides it,
from 'or for his sister.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:7. The גמרא stops here to quote the ברייתא that learns this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּתְהֵא קְבוּרַת מֵת מִצְוָה דּוֹחָה שַׁבָּת מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic about what overrides שבת, connected to 'execution does not override שבת' in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש proposes that burying a מת מצוה should override שבת by a קל וחומר from Temple service.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a discussion of which מצוות rank above others: שבת, Temple service, and burying a מת מצוה.

steps.title: A ברייתא asks why the נזיר verse lists four relatives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source that a מת מצוה overrides Temple service. The ברייתא quotes the verse forbidding a נזיר to become טמא for his father, mother, brother, or sister, and asks why all four are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "For his father, or for his mother, for his brother, or for his sister." Why does the verse need to say all of these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove a piece of ריש לקיש's קל וחומר: that burying a מת מצוה is stronger than Temple service. The ברייתא opens by asking why the verse lists so many relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have just said that a נזיר may not become טמא for a dead body. Listing four specific relatives looks like extra words, so the ברייתא asks "מה תלמוד לומר". The extra words will be used to teach a new law about a מת מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא. This brings an outside teaching as a source.
A person who has taken a vow that, among other things, forbids him to become טמא from a dead body.
Why does the verse need to say this? This points out words that seem extra.
A dead person with no one else to bury him. Whoever finds him must bury him.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "For his father, or for his mother,
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:7. The verse is talking about a נזיר, who may not become טמא even for these close relatives.

phrases.english: for his brother, or for his sister" —
why does the verse need to say this?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the middle link of ריש לקיש's קל וחומר: that a מת מצוה overrides Temple service.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that burying a מת מצוה overrides Temple service.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the extra relatives in the נזיר verse, במדבר 6:7.

steps.title: The ברייתא describes a man going to bring his קרבן פסח or circumcise his son
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins its answer with a case: a man who is on his way to slaughter his קרבן פסח or to circumcise his son. The ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, a man was going to slaughter his קרבן פסח or to circumcise his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts answering its own question by setting up a case. This line only sets the scene. What happens to this man comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two missions chosen, the קרבן פסח and ברית מילה, are very serious מצוות. If the verse will teach that a מת מצוה comes before even these, that shows how strong the duty to bury a מת מצוה is. That is exactly what ריש לקיש needs.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרבן פסח, the Passover offering brought in the בית המקדש.
To circumcise, meaning to do ברית מילה.
For example, if a person... This opens a case.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the ברייתא. The case is only being set up here, and the ruling about the מת מצוה comes right after.

phrases.english: Consider one who was going
to slaughter his Paschal offering
or to circumcise his son

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ לִשְׁחוֹט אֶת פִּסְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the ברייתא's question about why the verse lists the relatives.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: So far it only sets up the case of a man going to do two major מצוות. The ruling that comes out of the verse follows on the next amud.
